subject: weather balloons
title: What If You Tied 42 Weather Balloons to a Lawn Chair? In 1982 a Man Did

scenes.text: What if you tied weather balloons to a lawn chair? In 1982 one man tried it.
July 2nd, Los Angeles. A truck driver straps 42 helium balloons, each eight feet wide, to a Sears lawn chair.
The plan: hover about a hundred feet up for an hour. Instead, he shoots up to sixteen thousand feet.
He's now in airliner territory. Pilots from TWA and Delta radio in a man in a chair.
After about 45 minutes he starts shooting balloons with a pellet gun. Then he drops the gun.
He sinks into power lines in Long Beach, cutting power for twenty minutes. He walks away unharmed, and is fined 1,500 dollars.

description:
What if you tied weather balloons to a lawn chair? On 2 July 1982 a truck driver in San Pedro, Los Angeles, attached 42 eight-foot helium weather balloons to an aluminium lawn chair, planning to float about 100 feet up.
He rose to roughly 16,000 feet instead, where airline pilots reported him to air traffic control. He came down by shooting balloons with a pellet gun and landed in power lines in Long Beach, causing a 20-minute blackout. He was unhurt; the FAA fined him 4,000 dollars, later reduced to 1,500.
